reasons: Admin-initiated password resets and security-info changes are a fair proxy for the quoted 'reset passwords and/or transfer MFA tokens' help-desk step. However, the title promises a 'sign-in from new IP' that the query never tests, and the Actor != Target filter drops the follow-on self-registration of attacker MFA after takeover.

The query will mostly run, but three things weaken it. `ResultType == 0` compares SigninLogs' string ResultType to a long, so use "0". The join on TargetUpn == UserPrincipalName is case-sensitive with no tolower(), so real matches can be missed. The audit Result column is projected but never filtered to success, so failed admin attempts get joined too.

An analyst can run this today, but the summarize discards UserAgent and RiskLevelDuringSignIn, which were projected for triage. There is also no ActorIp-vs-SigninIp or baseline-IP comparison. Nearly every legitimate reset is followed by a sign-in within 4h, so the output is effectively a list of all help-desk resets.

The false positives listed (lost phone, onboarding, normal post-reset sign-in) are accurate, and a confidence of 40 is in range. But the title over-claims a new-IP condition that only exists in the tuning notes, and the draft doesn't acknowledge that the query will return nearly every admin reset across a large estate.
